report:
## Conclusion

Current evidence does **not clearly show that hypnosis is more effective than other methods for quitting smoking**, though it may be somewhat better than no treatment at all. The most rigorous evidence synthesis, the Cochrane systematic review (Barnes et al., updated 2019), found the trials on hypnotherapy for smoking cessation to be small, methodologically weak, and inconsistent, concluding there was **insufficient evidence to determine whether hypnotherapy is more effective than other cessation approaches or no treatment**, and no reliable data supporting recommendation of hypnotherapy as a stand‑alone smoking cessation aid (cochranelibrary.com/cdsr/doi/10.1002/14651858.CD004407.pub4/full).

A broader 2023 overview of meta-analyses on hypnosis across health conditions similarly reported mixed results for smoking specifically—of six effect estimates drawn from five reviews (including three Cochrane reviews), only two reached statistical significance, with effect sizes ranging from small to moderate (d = 0.12–0.84) (frontiersin.org/journals/psychology/articles/10.3389/fpsyg.2023.1330238/full).

More recent, less rigorous reviews present a more optimistic picture. A 2024/2025 systematic review in the *International Journal of Clinical and Experimental Hypnosis* concluded that "the efficacy of hypnotherapy for smoking cessation is positive," while cautioning that more studies using biologically confirmed abstinence are needed (tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/00207144.2024.2434082). A companion 2024 Frontiers paper comparing hypnotherapy to CBT likewise noted popularity among smokers but stated efficacy "cannot be considered sufficiently proven due to significant methodological limitations" (frontiersin.org/journals/psychology/articles/10.3389/fpsyg.2024.1330362/full).

**Bottom line:** Hypnosis may help some people, but robust, high-quality trial evidence supporting it as a proven, standalone smoking-cessation treatment is lacking. Evidence-based methods like nicotine replacement therapy, varenicline, and behavioral counseling remain better supported.
